items.title: Reflexive modules are torsion free and the double dual map is injective exactly for finite torsion free modules
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the basic comparison between reflexivity and torsion freeness over a domain (statement lines 5165-5174): a reflexive module is torsion free, and for a finite module M the natural map j to the double dual has torsion kernel and cokernel and is injective if and only if M is torsion free. The proof is a 42-line argument (proof lines 5177-5218) in which the interesting half is the finite case: the author chooses a partial system of generators whose images form a basis of M tensor K, writes the remaining generators in that basis over the fraction field, clears denominators with one element c to obtain two maps alpha and beta between R^r and M whose composites are multiplication by c, and then draws a commutative diagram with four occurrences of j to conclude that the kernel and cokernel of j are annihilated by c. The final step for (3) reads injectivity of j off the injectivity of beta. No step is left to the reader and the only cited input is the preceding lemma of the same section.
